THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.t: THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.short: She sells tomatoes... She steals destiny. Ama Mensah 22, poor tomato seller at Kaneshie, watches customers leave her for Madam Darkoa whose tomatoes glow green and never spoil. Her blind grandmother shouts: This is not tomato, this is destiny!
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.long: Kaneshie Market, 4am. Ama Mensah, 22, beautiful hardworking tomato seller from Agbogbloshie, feeds her blind grandmother Grandma Esi and jobless brother Kofi. When strange old woman Madam Darkoa appears selling glowing red tomatoes that never spoil, Ama's business dies. Blind Grandma Esi touches one and screams it is destiny theft - each tomato is a trapped human star. 99 destinies already trapped, Ama will be number 100. With Mallam Musah's black soap and white handkerchief, Ama must sell the cursed tomato back to the Market Witch on Tuesday full market day. Green lightning, yellow glowing eyes, blood inside tomato - Ghanaian spiritual folk tale about envy, hard work and destiny. Pure Ghana names, Kaneshie, Agbogbloshie, Makola. Moral: Not every shining business is clean.
THE MARKET WITCH - KANESHIE MARKET WITCH.full:
NARRATOR: Kaneshie Market, 4am, dark, cold, only torch lights. Ama Mensah, 22 years, beautiful, hardworking, very poor tomato seller, carries heavy basket on head from Agbogbloshie.

AMA MENSAH: Grandma Esi, today I will sell all my tomatoes by God's grace. I am tired of poverty. Kofi trotro no work, you blind, I am the only one. But I will not steal, I will not do juju. I will work hard with clean hands.

GRANDMA ESI: My granddaughter Ama, my spirit is not comfortable today. I am blind with eyes but I see with spirit. Not all red is tomato. Not all shining market is clean. Some traders sell more than goods. They sell destiny. Be careful in Kaneshie today.

NARRATOR: Same market, Madam Darkoa, 53, The Market Witch, sells reddest tomatoes that glow green at night and never spoil. Customers leave Ama.

AMA MENSAH: Why customers no dey buy from me today? My tomatoes fresh from Agbogbloshie this morning. Something is wrong.

AFIA: Ama, make I try buy one from Madam Darkoa and see. Maybe her own get chemical?

GRANDMA ESI: AHHHH! This is not tomato! This is destiny! This is human star! She is stealing people's stars!

GRANDMA ESI: That woman is a market witch! In 1973, she was cursed by Nana Okomfo for using 3 children for money rituals at Tano River. When you eat her tomato, she exchanges your good luck for her bad luck.

AFIA: Too late Grandma! I ate yesterday! My boyfriend broke up, my hair falling, my GHC 200 disappeared!

AMA MENSAH: I must confront her! Tonight midnight at Kaneshie when market empty!

NARRATOR: Midnight, 12:05am, empty Kaneshie Market. Ama hides behind Queen Yaa stall. Sees Madam Darkoa holding floating tomato with green lightning, chanting.

MADAM DARKOA: Give me your market... give me your marriage... give me your children... give me your womb... I give you tomatoes...

MADAM DARKOA: You small girl... you want to know my secret? Come closer. Buy one tomato. Just one.

NARRATOR: Ama runs to Makola to Mallam Musah, 80 years old.

MALLAM MUSAH: Ama Mensah, your destiny star already dim. You touched her stall last week. She started taking small small. Take black soap and white handkerchief. Don't eat anything in market for 7 days. Bring me one glowing tomato at 12 midnight on 7th day.

NARRATOR: 7th day, midnight, heavy rain. Ama steals one tomato. Tomato heavy like stone, cold like ice, inside baby crying.

AMA MENSAH: Eiii! This tomato heavy! I hear baby crying inside! Blood comes out, not water!

MALLAM MUSAH: Look! Each tomato is trapped destiny! She trapped 99 destinies. You will be number 100 and she will become young again!

NARRATOR: Meanwhile Kofi, Ama brother, greedy, jobless, goes to Madam Darkoa.

KOFI: Madam Darkoa, make me rich. I will bring you my sister.

MADAM DARKOA: Bring Ama hair and pant. I will make you rich in one night.

KOFI: Forgive me sister, I need money.

AMA MENSAH: Dreaming, woman with green hands strangling her.

MALLAM MUSAH: Only one way left. Kofi betrayed you. She has your pant. You must sell cursed tomato back to her on Tuesday market day, when market fullest, when queen mother Queen Yaa is there.

NARRATOR: Tuesday, Kaneshie full like Christmas. Queen Yaa inspecting stalls. Ama holding cursed tomato wrapped in white handkerchief.

AMA MENSAH: Madam Darkoa, good morning. I want to sell you tomato. Very fresh. Better than yours.

MADAM DARKOA: You small girl want to sell tomato to tomato seller? Give me.

MADAM DARKOA: AHHH! WHAT HAVE YOU DONE!

NARRATOR: Green lightning explodes from Madam Darkoa mouth, eyes, hands! Throat glows green, skin cracks like rotten tomato. All trapped destinies fly out as bright green lights. Market women who poor suddenly get customers.

MADAM DARKOA: If I go down, you go down with me!

AMA MENSAH: I reject you in Jesus name and Allah name! Kaneshie market is for hard work, not witchcraft!

GRANDMA ESI: Return to where you came from, witch! 

NARRATOR: GBOOOM! Madam Darkoa melts into pile of rotten tomatoes, green smoke to sky. Only her stall burns with green fire.

QUEEN YAA: From today, Madam Darkoa spot given to Ama Mensah for bravery! We pray every Monday!

KOFI: Ama, forgive me, I was greedy.

AMA MENSAH: I forgive you brother, but return GHC 5000 to Mallam Musah.

NARRATOR: One month later, Ama biggest tomato business in Kaneshie. Mr Joseph gives her cold store. She marries Mr Joseph son. At night, when Ama closes stall, sometimes she still sees one green tomato glowing under Madam Darkoa old table... She never touches it. THE END.

MORAL: Not every shining business clean. Hard work with small profit better than quick money that steals future.

SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.t: SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.short: 22-year-old Choima from Onitsha sells zobo to pay her sick mother's N450k hospital bill. An agent promises $500/month house help job in Saudi. But she is sold for $4000, passport seized, phone taken, forced to work 19 hours daily as a slave.
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.long: Nollywood drama about human trafficking and Saudi housemaid wahala. Choima, beautiful Anambra girl from Onitsha Main Market, pays N350k to agent Alhaja Kudirat for Riyadh job. No contract, no NAPTIP clearance, passport collected at Lagos airport. In Saudi, madam Mama Um Khalid seizes phone, locks gate, beats her, no salary for 6 months. Based on true stories of Nigerian girls in Saudi, NAPTIP warning, illegal migration from Anambra to Saudi Arabia. Pure Igbo names, Onitsha, Agege training house, Murtala Muhammed Airport, Riyadh, Jeddah. Moral: Not every abroad is greener, verify agent.
SAUDI WAHALA - THEY SOLD ME FOR $4000.full:
NARRATOR: Onitsha Main Market, Anambra. Noon. Hot sun. Choima, 22, beautiful, fair-skinned, natural hair, sells zobo and meat pie to feed four younger brothers and sisters. Father died. Mother sick, leg swollen, on mat at home.

CHOIMA: Mama, I will sell everything today. I need N450,000 for your hospital at Nnamdi Azikiwe Teaching Hospital. God will provide.

MAMA CHOIMA: [crying] My daughter, don't stress. I am tired.

NARRATOR: A black Lexus parks. Alhaja Kudirat steps out. Gold, expensive lace.

ALHAJA KUDIRAT: My daughter, you are beautiful and hardworking. I have house help job in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Salary $500 per month, almost N800,000. Many Nigerian girls are there enjoying. They drive Benz.

CHOIMA: Aunty, I saw on TikTok they beat house helps in Saudi. My friend from Asaba went and never came back.

ALHAJA KUDIRAT: That is Dubai, not Saudi. Saudi is good Islamic country. Very safe. My daughter is there. Look [shows video of girl dancing in Riyadh mall].

NARRATOR: Choima thinks of mother crying, brothers not in school, shop rent unpaid. She says yes. Sells mother's wrapper shop, borrows from church, pays N350,000 processing fee.

NARRATOR: Lagos, Agege, small house, 2 weeks training. Clean toilet with hands, wear abaya, say Naam Mama. No contract. No NAPTIP paper. No embassy meeting.

NARRATOR: Murtala Muhammed Airport. Alhaja collects passport.

ALHAJA KUDIRAT: I will keep it safe. Your madam will give you Iqama.

NARRATOR: First airplane ever. Lagos to Jeddah to Riyadh, 6 hours, black abaya, crying. Riyadh Airport, Mama Um Khalid, 50 years, big, seven children, three-storey house, collects phone.

MAMA UM KHALID: No phone. No Nigerian boyfriend. Only work.

NARRATOR: Her room is a small store. No bed. Thin mat beside rice bags. No fan. Day 1 suffering: Wake 4am, cook breakfast for ten, clean 5 bedrooms, 4 toilets, wash clothes by hand, cook Kabsa for fifteen, watch five children, wash plates midnight. 5am to 1am. Nineteen hours daily. Feet swollen.

MAMA UM KHALID: Yalla! Yalla! Fast! Donkey! [beats with mop stick]

CHOIMA: [crying inside toilet she cleans] God, in Onitsha I was free.

CHOIMA: Mama, please my salary? My mother is sick in Anambra.

MAMA UM KHALID: Salary after three months! I paid your agent $4000 for you! You are my property now!

NARRATOR: Choima understands. Alhaja sold her for $4000. She is not worker. She is slave. Three months, no salary, no phone, passport seized, gate locked with camera, Iqama not done.

NARRATOR: Sixth month, night, madam's 20-year-old son tries to enter her small store room.

CHOIMA: [screams, bites hand, locks door] Leave me!

NARRATOR: Reports to madam. Madam beats her again.

MAMA UM KHALID: You seducing my son! Bad Nigerian girl! [locks her outside in 48-degree heat, no water whole day]

CHOIMA: [kneeling outside in hot sun, black abaya, sweating, looking at sky] God, I left Anambra to help my mother. Now I am slave in Saudi. Who will save me? [hides small paper in underwear, number copied from airport toilet wall: +966 11 442 8624 Nigerian Embassy Riyadh]

NARRATOR: Night. Whisper through fence. Fatima from Ibadan, next compound.

FATIMA: Choima, don't cry. Many Nigerian girls here one year no salary. We will run to embassy together on Friday when madam goes to mosque...

TO BE CONTINUED IN PART 2 - THE FRIDAY ESCAPE.

HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.t: HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DAY
HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.short: Adaeze's Lagos wedding with 400 guests turns to chaos. At 6am on wedding day, she catches fiancé Emeka naked with her younger sister Chiamaka on their wedding bed. He says she is boring. She takes microphone and shocks everyone.
HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.long: Nigerian wedding betrayal story Lagos, 400 guests, bride catches groom sleeping with sister on wedding day. Adaeze was to marry Emeka in Lekki Lagos, white wedding gown, 400 guests already seated. Emeka slept with her blood sister Chiamaka 10 minutes before wedding. She records confession, plays on microphone, walks out as queen. Based on true Lagos wedding wahala, sister betrayal, fiancé cheating. Pure Nigerian names, Lekki, Lagos, Dangote contract. Moral: Sisterhood, self-worth. High search: Nigeria wedding betrayal story, sister slept with my fiancé on wedding day, Lagos wedding scandal.
HE SLEPT WITH MY SISTER ON MY WEDDING DA.full:
NARRATOR: Lagos, 6am, wedding day. Adaeze, 26, beautiful, in white wedding gown, makeup done, 400 guests already seated in hall outside. Tradition: go pray with fiancé before wedding.

ADAEZE: [knocks] Emeka, baby, let's pray before we go to church.

NARRATOR: Door locked. Moaning inside. Adaeze pushes door hard. Sees it. Fiancé Emeka, naked, on top of her own younger sister Chiamaka, in their wedding bed.

ADAEZE: Jesus Christ! Emeka! Chiamaka! What is this!

CHIAMAKA: [shouts, covering body] Sister please, it's not what you think! He forced me!

EMEKA: [looks at Adaeze, no shame] Adaeze, you were always too boring in bed. Your sister taught me yesterday what you couldn't in 3 years.

NARRATOR: Wedding in 3 hours. Mother dancing outside, spraying money. Adaeze standing in wedding gown, watching sister dress quickly, crying.

NARRATOR: Adaeze walks to hall. White gown dragging. Makeup smudged with tears. DJ playing. Mother dancing with aunties. Everyone shouting Omo iyawo ti de!

ADAEZE: [collects microphone, DJ stops music, voice shaking] Good morning everyone. Thank you for coming to my wedding. But there will be no wedding today.

NARRATOR: Silence. 400 people quiet.

MAMA ADAEZE: Adaeze! What are you saying?!

ADAEZE: [points at entrance] This man Emeka that I was supposed to marry, I caught him 10 minutes ago sleeping with my own blood sister Chiamaka. On my wedding bed. On my wedding day.

NARRATOR: Hall scatters! Jesu! Ewo! Oloriburuku! Mother faints.

CHIAMAKA: [runs, kneels, holds Adaeze leg] Sister, he forced me! He said if I don't sleep with him, he will cancel wedding and disgrace you!

EMEKA: [laughs] So? At least now you know truth. I never loved you, Adaeze. I only wanted your father's land in Lekki. Your sister is sweeter.

ADAEZE: [raises phone, red light blinking]

EMEKA: What recording? You bluffing.

ADAEZE: [plays loud on microphone] EMEKA VOICE: You were always too boring in bed. Your sister taught me yesterday what you couldn't in 3 years.

NARRATOR: Two police officers, father's friends for security, walk in. Papa Adaeze stands, agbada shaking.

PAPA ADAEZE: Emeka, I gave you my daughter, and you repay me like this?

EMEKA: [kneels instantly] Sir, please! It was devil! Adaeze, biko, forgive me!

ADAEZE: [looks at both, tears but smiling] Officers, don't arrest him. Let him go.

EVERYONE: WHAT?!

ADAEZE: Let him go, because real punishment is he will watch me become millionaire without him. And Chiamaka, you will never enter my house again until you learn what sisterhood means.

NARRATOR: Adaeze removes wedding gown in front of everyone, wears jeans under it, walks out of own wedding hall like queen.

NARRATOR: 3 months later. Emeka loses job. Chiamaka comes begging. Adaeze gets contract with Dangote.

NARRATOR: Last week, Emeka sends text.

EMEKA: Adaeze, I am dying. Please come see me. I have secret about Chiamaka you need to know...
